abstract: |
  Every full-sided Mahjong wait on $3n$ ranks with $m$ melds has each
  multiplicity at most $3(m-n)+1$. For $n\ge2$ this bound is attained at every
  permitted meld count. Thus the exact copy cap at which all such waits are
  live, and their count stabilizes, is $3(m-n)+2$. We prove the bound by
  removing a common triplet, and check the argument in Lean.

## Fixing the meld count {#sec-question}

Use the model of @xue-zhong-2026: a hand $c=(c_1,\ldots,c_{3n})$ has
$3m+1$ tiles before drawing. It is a full-sided wait when every rank can be
drawn to complete $m$ melds and a pair. A meld is a triplet or three consecutive
ranks. A physical copy cap $q$ makes every draw live precisely when

$$
c_i+1\le q\qquad(1\le i\le3n).
$$ {#eq-live}

The [existence note](arbitrary-cap.html) allows $n,m,q$ to vary and asks
whether at least one live hand exists. Here we fix $n,m$ and ask how large
$q$ must be to admit **every** full-sided wait. Assume $n\ge1$ and $m>n$,
the permitted range for an unrestricted full wait.

::: {#thm-coordinate}
## A uniform coordinate bound

Every full-sided $(n,m)$-wait satisfies

$$
c_i\le3(m-n)+1\qquad(1\le i\le3n).
$$

For $n\ge2$, some full wait attains equality.
:::

Let $F(n,m)$ be the number of full waits without a physical copy cap, and
$L_q(n,m)$ the number that are live at cap $q$. These are finite counts of
labelled multiplicity vectors; reflected hands are not identified.

::: {#thm-stability}
## The exact stabilization cap

For $n\ge2$ and $m>n$, the following are equivalent:

1. Every full-sided $(n,m)$-wait is live at cap $q$.
2. $L_q(n,m)=F(n,m)$.
3. $q\ge3(m-n)+2$.

Below this threshold, $L_q(n,m)<F(n,m)$.
:::

At order one, the [three-rank note](three-ranks.html) gives the slightly
smaller sharp threshold $q=3m-2$. The bound in @thm-coordinate remains valid
there, but can be improved by one.

## A large coordinate leaves little elsewhere {#sec-excess}

Put $d=m-n$. Write $b=(0,1,\ldots,1,0)$ for the interior-one hand.
The interior-positivity theorem gives $c_i\ge b_i$, so the excess
$e=c-b$ is nonnegative and has total mass

$$
\begin{aligned}
\sum_i e_i&=(3m+1)-(3n-2)\\
&=3d+3.
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-excess}

Suppose the coordinate bound fails, so $c_i\ge3d+2$. Since $b_i\le1$,
we have $e_i\ge3d+1$. @eq-excess leaves at most two excess tiles
at every other rank, and hence

$$
c_j\le3\qquad(j\ne i).
$$ {#eq-sparse}

This sparse configuration is what allows a triplet at $i$ to be removed
simultaneously from all winning draws.

## Why the triplet is common to every draw {#sec-removal}

At the least possible meld count $m=n+1$, the structural classification
already gives $c_i\le4$, which is @thm-coordinate in this case.
For the inductive step, $d\ge2$ and therefore $c_i\ge8$.

Draw any rank $p$ and choose a winning pair at rank $r$. After removing
the pair, the meldable hand

$$
h=c+\boldsymbol e_p-2\boldsymbol e_r
$$

still has $h_i\ge6$. Use its canonical meld placement, whose sequence
coefficient at each starting position is at most two. If this placement
has no triplet at $i$, the three incident sequence coefficients account
for at most six tiles there. Since $h_i\ge6$, all three coefficients must
equal two. In particular the two distinct neighbouring ranks exist and satisfy

$$
h_{i-1}\ge4,\qquad h_{i+1}\ge4.
$$

But @eq-sparse says every rank other than $i$ had at most three tiles
before drawing. Removing a pair cannot increase a multiplicity; only the
single drawn rank $p$ could reach four. Two distinct neighbours cannot
both be that rank. This contradiction forces a canonical triplet at $i$.

Thus each winning decomposition admits removal of the same triplet
$3\boldsymbol e_i$. The hand $c'=c-3\boldsymbol e_i$ is a full-sided
$(n,m-1)$-wait. Induction gives

$$
c_i-3=c'_i\le3((m-1)-n)+1,
$$

which rearranges to @thm-coordinate. This is induction on the meld count,
using the structural base classification; it does not enumerate candidate
higher-meld hands.

## A family attaining the bound {#sec-extremal}

For $n\ge2$, take the classified hand
$B_n=b+3\boldsymbol e_1+3\boldsymbol e_{3n-3}$.
It is a full wait with $n+1$ melds and has four tiles at rank $3n-3$.
Adding any triplet preserves every winning draw. Consequently

$$
c=b+3\boldsymbol e_1+3(m-n)\boldsymbol e_{3n-3}
$$ {#eq-witness}

is a full-sided $(n,m)$-wait, and $c_{3n-3}=3(m-n)+1$.
This proves sharpness in @thm-coordinate. For example, at $n=3,m=5$
the hand is

$$
(3,1,1,1,1,7,1,1,0).
$$

It is live at cap eight and excluded at cap seven.

@eq-live and the coordinate bound make every full wait live at
$q\ge3(m-n)+2$. Below this threshold the hand in @eq-witness is missing.
The unrestricted full-wait set is finite: every coordinate is a nonnegative
integer bounded by @thm-coordinate. A proper subset therefore has strictly
smaller cardinality, proving @thm-stability as a statement about counts too.

::: {#cor-eight}
## All eight hands become live at cap five

For $n\ge2$ and $m=n+1$, the live count is zero for $q\le3$, one for
$q=4$, and eight for every $q\ge5$.
:::

The earlier minimum-cap result excludes $q\le3$. The classification gives
the unique cap-four live hand and eight unrestricted full waits. The new
threshold $3((n+1)-n)+2=5$ then admits all eight.

The [bounded-core counting note](triplet-counting.html) expresses the unrestricted
count using finite core data and proves its eventual polynomial behavior.

## Checked Lean source {#sec-lean}

[CopyCapStability.lean](CopyCapStability.lean) proves the coordinate bound,
an extremal witness, the sharp uniform cap, strict inequality of counts
below it, and the count of eight at cap five or above. The triplet-removal
and finiteness arguments are included in the same module.

The sources use Lean 4.35.0 against the structural library at
[this revision](https://github.com/lunaluteus/ninegates-lean4/tree/7b379afe7f54f34c59c8abdfc8e6fa5f0bee952a).
From this SunQuarTeX checkout, run:

```sh
uv run python examples/live-waits/check-lean.py \
  --library /path/to/ninegates-lean4
```

The [checker](check-lean.py) compiles nineteen source modules in a fresh temporary
directory with strict linters, then audits 134 declarations. Only
`propext`, `Classical.choice`, and `Quot.sound` are permitted. Rendering the
document is separate from checking the proofs. These notes remain an
independent experiment in this fork.
